deep.reconstruction:
The sheet is written upside down relative to the scan. It is a working page that derives a linear recurrence for a doubly indexed coefficient array a_{mu,nu}, together with a few trigonometric side calculations. The trigonometric calculations show that the a_{mu,nu} are coefficients of a double expansion of the form Sum a_{mu,nu} (something)^mu (a cos nu phi + b sin nu phi), with a factor 2 cos psi coupling neighbouring indices.

(1) Side column (left), routine trigonometry used to shift the index nu:
- [a cos(nu+1)phi + b sin(nu+1)phi] + [a cos(nu-1)phi + b sin(nu-1)phi] = 2 cos phi (a cos nu phi + b sin nu phi). It is written once with cos psi and once with cos phi.
- The difference version, 'a cos(nu+1)phi + b sin(nu+1)phi - (a cos(nu-1)phi + b sin(nu-1)phi)', is also entered.
- The phi-derivative d/dphi (a cos nu phi + b sin nu phi) = nu(-a sin nu phi + b cos nu phi).
So multiplying the series by 2cos(angle) moves a coefficient from nu to nu+1 and nu-1. This is why every a_{mu-1,nu+-1} on the page carries a factor 2 cos psi.

(2) Notation. Riemann writes mu_2, (mu-1)_2, (nu+1)_2, etc. The factorisations on the page are consistent with x_2 = x(x-1) (my inference; possibly x(x-1)/2 up to a constant factor):
- mu_2 - nu_2 = (mu-nu)(mu+nu-1)
- mu_2 - (nu+1)_2 = (mu-nu-1)(mu+nu)
- (mu-1)_2 - (nu+1)_2 = (mu-nu-2)(mu+nu-1). This matches the line '-(mu-nu-2)(mu+nu-1)' directly under the a_{mu-1,nu+1} entry.
- (mu-1)_2 - nu_2 = (mu-nu-1)(mu+nu-2)
- (mu-1)_2 - (nu-1)_2 = (mu-nu)(mu+nu-3)
The bracket (-nu-1 + mu-1 - (mu-1)_2 + (nu+1)_2) simplifies to (mu-nu-2)(2-mu-nu). This is what the line '(mu-nu-2) - (mu-nu-2) mu+nu ...' is doing.

(3) Main relation (middle block). The leading coefficient is
(mu-nu)(mu+nu)(mu-nu-1)(mu+nu-1) a_{mu,nu} = (mu_2-nu_2)(mu_2-(nu+1)_2) a_{mu,nu}.
It is related to the two terms
+-2cos psi (mu-nu)(mu-nu-1)(mu+nu-2)_2 a_{mu-1,nu-1}
and
-2cos psi (mu+nu)(mu+nu-1)(mu-nu-2)_2 a_{mu-1,nu+1},
where (k)_2 = k(k-1).

An earlier attempt with factors (nu-1)(mu+nu-2)(mu-nu) and (nu-1)(mu+nu)(mu-nu-2) is struck out.

The lower block assembles the pieces. Terms of the form [(mu-1)_2-(nu+-1)_2]·(mu-1)·(2 a_{mu-1,nu+-1} cos psi) and [(mu-1)_2-(nu+-1)_2]·(nu+-1)·(+-2 a_{mu-1,nu+-1} cos psi) come from applying a second-order operator and the cos-shift. The operator has 'eigenvalue' mu_2 - nu_2 on the mu,nu term, suggesting an Euler/Laplace-type operator in r and phi; this is my inference.

(4) Top block. The procedure is iterated one level further, expressing things through a_{mu-2,nu+2} and a_{mu-3,nu+1} with factors like (mu-2)_2-(nu+2)_2, (mu-3)_2(nu+1)_2 and (-2cos psi).

(5) Bottom right. A rhombus diagram of index pairs shows the dependency lattice after repeated application: a_{mu,nu}; a_{mu-1,nu+1}, a_{mu-1,nu-1}; a_{mu-2,nu+2}, a_{mu-2,nu}, a_{mu-2,nu-2}; a_{mu-3,nu+1}, a_{mu-3,nu-1}; a_{mu-4,nu}. This is a Pascal-like propagation in which each step lowers mu by 1 and shifts nu by +-1.

Purpose. Most likely a power/Fourier double-series solution of a linear PDE with a direction-dependent (cos psi) coefficient. The previous page treats a fourth-order (plate/elasticity-type) equation, so a fourth-order operator is plausible, since the leading coefficient is a product of two quadratic factors. The exact equation is not recoverable from this page.
errors: The coefficients of a_{mu-1,nu+-1} assembled in the lower block, e.g. [(mu-1)_2-(nu-1)_2]((mu-1)+(nu-1)) = (mu-nu)(mu+nu-3)(mu+nu-2), do not obviously coincide with the cleaned-up middle-block form (mu-nu)(mu-nu-1)(mu+nu-2)(mu+nu-3). An extra factor or an additional term is involved that is not visible on the page, so the two blocks cannot be confirmed to agree without the governing equation.
Riemann himself struck out one version of the a_{mu-1,nu+-1} coefficients (factors (nu-1)(mu+nu-2)(mu-nu), etc.), indicating a corrected slip.

The first lines (a_{mu-3,nu+1} with (mu+nu-2)(mu-nu-4)(mu-nu-2)) are too faint to verify. With x_2 = x(x-1), (mu-3)_2-(nu+1)_2 = (mu-nu-4)(mu+nu-3), so the transcribed factor (mu+nu-2) may be a misreading or a different combination.

results.what: Index-shift identity a cos(n+1)phi + b sin(n+1)phi + a cos(n-1)phi + b sin(n-1)phi = 2cos phi (a cos n phi + b sin n phi), and the derivative of a cos n phi + b sin n phi
Two-index linear recurrence for double-series coefficients a_{mu,nu}, with leading factor (mu-nu)(mu+nu)(mu-nu-1)(mu+nu-1) and coupling through 2cos psi to a_{mu-1,nu+-1}, plus the dependency rhombus
results.modern_name: Frobenius-type / method of undetermined coefficients for a double (power x Fourier) series solution of a linear PDE
